mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to anticipated economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rose by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as companies anticipate lower revenues.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS declined for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% within a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as markets react to improved economic activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs in a month signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 jobs in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% in a month and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (change < 0.2%), it signals a robust demand without inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 10% in 1 month AND CPIAUCSL change < 0.2%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST increased by more than 10% and CPIAUCSL change was less than 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased over a 3-month period.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 1% in a month and GDP (GDPC1) shows growth above 2% in the same quarter, it signals a robust supply side and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases > 1% in 1 month AND GDPC1 growth > 2% in the same quarter
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% and GDPC1 growth was above 2%.
